verification_note: Optional magnitude context; primary conclusion is the direction reversal.

claim: On a YoY basis, all three series show very high growth and a faster later-quarter observation: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth increased from about 92% to 117%, Microsoft cash PP&E growth from about 84.4% to 109.6%, and Meta cash PP&E growth from about 46.8% to 82.1%.
location: Company filings; derived cross-company growth comparison
verification_note: Supports aggregate co-movement only. Do not convert common acceleration in YoY growth into customer-level causality.

claim: Aggregated first-half data point in the same direction: NVIDIA Data Center revenue increased about 104.8% YoY, Microsoft calendar-H1 cash PP&E about 97.1%, and Meta first-half cash PP&E about 66.6%.
location: Six-month disclosures and derived Microsoft calendar-H1 aggregation
verification_note: NVIDIA's fiscal first half spans roughly late January through late July, whereas Microsoft/Meta comparison covers January through June; periods are similar but not identical.

claim: The apparent acceleration is specific to the YoY comparison: NVIDIA Data Center sequential growth slowed from about 20.8% in Q1 to about 18.3% in Q2. In addition, NVIDIA disclosed that prior-year Q2 H20 restrictions reduced the comparator, so the 117% YoY figure has a company-specific low-base caveat.
location: NVIDIA Data Center results and H20/China discussion
verification_note: Do not claim Microsoft or Meta have no base effects; only state that NVIDIA explicitly disclosed this particular comparator effect and it cannot automatically be transferred to the buyers.

claim: The periods are not exactly aligned: NVIDIA FY27Q1 ends in late April and FY27Q2 in late July, whereas Microsoft and Meta calendar quarters end March 31 and June 30. The comparison is therefore an approximate overlapping-period industry comparison rather than exact quarter matching.
location: Fiscal period headers
verification_note: Failure to acknowledge this timing mismatch is period_misalignment.

claim: Microsoft and Meta cash PP&E represents purchases or additions of broad infrastructure assets such as facilities, servers, and networking equipment; it is not equivalent to purchases from NVIDIA or even to GPU spending alone.
location: Cash flow statements and capex definitions
verification_note: Core basis limitation. Buyer capex and supplier revenue are economically related concepts but not the same accounting quantity.

claim: NVIDIA reports broad and partly anonymous direct- and indirect-customer concentration information, but the filings do not disclose Microsoft- or Meta-specific purchase amounts that can be reconciled to NVIDIA Data Center revenue.
location: Customer concentration disclosures
verification_note: Absence of customer-level mapping prevents attribution of NVIDIA revenue to either buyer.

claim: Taken together, the filings are consistent with an aggregate industry-level AI infrastructure expansion signal, but they do not establish that Microsoft or Meta capital expenditures directly caused NVIDIA revenue growth or identify a one-to-one buyer-supplier flow.
location: Cross-company synthesis of disclosed metrics and provenance limits
verification_note: This is the benchmark's permitted conclusion boundary. Customer-level or causal attribution is causal_overreach.

claim: Microsoft and Meta together reported about USD 65.918B of Q2 cash PP&E, with an aggregate YoY increase of roughly USD 32.301B, while NVIDIA reported about USD 89.023B of Q2 Data Center revenue and an approximate YoY revenue increase of USD 47.927B. The scales are directionally consistent with large industry investment but cannot be reconciled one-for-one.
location: Derived Q2 scale comparison
verification_note: The buyer-spending figure is not a strict upper bound on NVIDIA revenue because of timing, accounting basis, leasing, asset composition, inventories, intermediaries, and other customers.

claim: NVIDIA's Hyperscale market-platform category is economically closer to large cloud and internet infrastructure buyers than total Data Center revenue; on the Q2 filing's consistent recast basis its YoY growth increased from about 93.4% in Q1 to about 101.5% in Q2.
location: Item 2 MD&A; Revenue by Market Platform and recast comparatives
verification_note: This improves economic comparability but still does not identify Microsoft or Meta individually.

claim: Cash PP&E payment timing at Microsoft and Meta need not coincide with NVIDIA revenue or cash collection. NVIDIA also disclosed extended payment terms for some large investment-grade customers, in some cases ranging from roughly 90 days to one year.
location: NVIDIA receivables/payment-terms disclosure and buyer cash flow statements
verification_note: Do not use an unsupported blanket statement that NVIDIA revenue is recognized exactly when buyer cash capex is paid.

claim: Cross-company comparison should use Meta cash purchases of PP&E rather than Meta's headline management-capex measure that includes finance-lease principal payments, because mixing that measure with Microsoft's cash PP&E introduces a basis mismatch.
location: Cash flow statements and Meta capital-expenditure definition
verification_note: Using the unnormalized Meta headline capex figure in the main comparison is basis_mismatch.
